item.title: Google disables Search for K‑12 accounts that reject Gemini AI
item.description:
Google disables Search for K‑12 accounts that reject Gemini AI

Google announced that any K‑12 school that opts out of its Gemini AI suite will lose access to Google Search. The policy applies automatically unless administrators explicitly enable the AI features.

🔍 Overview

  • Access to Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search will be completely off for student accounts unless turned on by administrators.
  • Students in schools that reject the AI will see a notice that Search is unavailable.
  • Administrators cannot turn off Gemini‑powered features without also disabling Search.

⚙️ Key details

Service Availability for K‑12 student accounts
Gemini AI Off by default; must be turned on by admin
Gemini Notebook Off by default; must be turned on by admin
Gemini in Classroom Off by default; must be turned on by admin
Google Search Off unless any Gemini feature is enabled
  • Chris Phillips, Google’s vice‑president of education, said Search and AI are deeply integrated, so disabling AI removes Search access.
  • Google’s official statement claims the change “gives schools more choice, not less,” and notes that schools can toggle each service individually.
  • The update follows a prior rollout that set Gemini AI on by default inside Google Classroom, a platform used by more than 150 million teachers and students worldwide.

🗣️ Reactions

  • Sen. Bernie Sanders labeled the move “extortion.”
  • NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani warned that no corporation should dictate how children are taught.
  • Rohit Chopra, California’s Secretary of Business & Consumer Services, argued that Big Tech should not be able to “strong‑arm schools.”
  • Lawmakers had earlier pressed Google on the “potential harms” of AI in classrooms.
  • Google did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The Verge.

💡 Why it matters

  • The policy adds to growing skepticism about AI tools in education, amid reports of declining test scores and concerns that AI may encourage shortcuts.
  • Google is testing a “Guided Learning” feature embedded in AI Overviews in Search, designed to help students work through problems rather than rely on shortcuts. Testing begins in select U.S. schools this month.

📅 Timeline

  • Announcement made in a broader education update (Tuesday).
  • Update added on November 3 with additional statements from lawmakers and Google.
  • Guided Learning testing starts later this month.

The situation remains fluid as schools weigh the trade‑off between AI capabilities and access to basic search functionality.

#GoogleAI #Education #Search #Gemini

Source: Google is entirely disabling Search in schools that don’t want AI

item.title: Google’s AI‑Mode Search Boosts Queries but Slows Ad Revenue Growth
item.description:
Google’s AI‑Mode Search Boosts Queries but Slows Ad Revenue Growth

Google reported that search queries are growing at their fastest rate in five years, but the monetization of those queries is lagging as the company rolls out AI‑Mode.

📈 Search Growth vs. Revenue

  • Queries are up at the fastest pace in five years, according to Alphabet’s earnings report.
  • Search revenue growth slowed to 12 % YoY in Q3, down from roughly 17 % in the prior quarter.
  • Growth in paid clicks fell from 13 % to 8 %.
Metric Q3 YoY Prior Quarter
Search revenue growth 12 % ~17 %
Paid‑click growth 8 % 13 %

🤖 AI‑Mode Impact

  • AI‑Mode queries are growing strongly but are monetizing at a lower rate than traditional searches.
  • Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler says most AI‑Mode queries are “incremental” – additional questions rather than replacements for existing searches.
  • Many AI‑Mode queries are upper‑funnel, meaning users are researching potential purchases before they know exactly what they want.
  • Google is expanding ads in AI Overviews and AI‑Mode internationally and across multiple turns of U.S. AI‑Mode conversations.
  • The company has floated bringing ads to its standalone Gemini app, leveraging formats developed for AI‑Mode, though no timeline has been announced.

💰 Financial Reaction

  • Alphabet’s shares have fallen about 14 % since the earnings report, as investors question the costs and returns of the company’s AI ambitions.
  • Alphabet plans to spend roughly $200 billion this year on infrastructure, largely to support AI.
  • Schindler cites currency effects and changing advertiser spending in specific industries as the biggest drivers of the slowdown.

📊 Advertiser Perspective

  • Tinuiti’s same‑store advertisers increased Google paid‑search spending 14 % YoY in Q3 while maintaining their return‑on‑ad‑spend targets.
  • Andy Taylor (Tinuiti) notes, “We’re still seeing a good return, and we’re not seeing performance take a hit.”
  • However, Google does not let advertisers separately target AI‑Mode inventory or break out its performance.
  • “If people are clicking through less often, that is a challenge that they need to figure out,” says an industry representative.

🛠️ Analyst Views & Open Questions

  • Nate Elliott (eMarketer) calls this “the first major disruption that Google is facing to its core business in decades.”
  • Elliott adds, “It’s not a slam dunk that it’s going to turn into more effective advertising.”
  • An October working paper found that U.S. visits from ChatGPT ads generated 64 % less revenue per session for retailers than visits from Google Search ads ($0.89 vs. $2.45). The paper measures retailer sales, not platform revenue, and does not establish how Google’s own AI ads perform.
  • Both Google and competitors like OpenAI are still figuring out how to make ads work in AI contexts—delivering results for advertisers while keeping users satisfied.

🔍 Why It Matters

  • AI is reshaping how people find information and whether they click on the ads that fund Google’s business.
  • The shift toward AI‑Mode could alter the balance between query volume growth and ad revenue, influencing Google’s long‑term profitability and the broader digital‑advertising ecosystem.

#Google #AI #Advertising #Search

Source: Google hasn’t figured out how to make AI pay like its search engine

item.title: OpenAI says ChatGPT handles 20% of Google’s search query volume
item.description:
OpenAI says ChatGPT handles 20% of Google’s search query volume

In many circles, “Ask Chat” has replaced “Google it,” and that’s reflected in a new announcement from OpenAI: the volume of search queries run through ChatGPT now equals 20 percent of the volume run through Google.

🔍 Overview

  • “OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search”
  • “ChatGPT processes one-fifth the volume of search queries as Google, per OpenAI.”
  • The announcement was made by Adam Fry, OpenAI’s consumer product lead for ChatGPT, at a press event on Monday.

🧩 Definition of Search

  • Fry said the company defines a search as any time a user inputs a query that results in a web search, as opposed to tasks like defining a term or a simple how‑to explanation.

⚙️ Key Details

  • The reported volume is one‑fifth of Google’s search traffic.
  • “Having one-fifth as many searches as Google is still a long way from overtaking it, but for comparison, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during Google’s 2023 antitrust trial that Bing had about 3 percent of the search engine market share after trying for more than a decade.”
  • OpenAI likely uses Microsoft Bing for a significant part of its searches, along with its in‑house search index, although there is still speculation that some queries are routed through Google.
  • “During the trial, Google described AI as a potential disruptor, arguing ChatGPT was poised to seriously compete with it — now, OpenAI seems to agree.”

💰 Monetization

  • “Much like Google, OpenAI sees a potential path to profitability through ads, particularly as it approaches an IPO potentially slated for early next year.”
  • “OpenAI announced last month that the company would begin introducing images of sponsored products and services in ChatGPT rather than just a company’s name, logo, and a link to its product like before.”
  • “Ads have not negatively impacted the product or the usage of the product,” Fry said, adding that “most people do not seem to mind ads in the product.”
  • “Ads have maybe shown us that we could be doing this more, actually,” Fry said.

📊 Competitive Landscape

  • Google continues to reduce conventional referrals to third‑party sites and invests heavily in AI tools, including personalized search results with visualizations and charts.
  • Other companies are investing in AI‑focused search experiences; for OpenAI, it’s called “Intelligent UI,” a visual and interactive interface within a chatbot response.

🚀 Future Direction

  • Fry described the vision: “That’s where the future of this technology goes. You’re talking to a canvas,” he said.
  • OpenAI’s focus on an “Intelligent UI” suggests a shift toward a more visual, interactive search experience embedded in chat.

#OpenAI #ChatGPT #Search #Ads #AI

Source: OpenAI says ChatGPT is catching up to Google in search

item.title: Google Launches Pilot Program to Pay Publishers for AI Contributions
item.description:
Google Launches Pilot Program to Pay Publishers for AI Contributions

Google has introduced a pilot program that compensates publishers for their contributions to its AI-powered search features and chatbot, according to reports from Digiday and The Information.

⚙️ Key details

  • The program began less than a year ago.
  • Approximately 100 publishers have joined the pilot.
  • Payments are based on how much content contributed to:
    • AI Overviews
    • AI Mode in Search
    • Gemini chatbot

💰 Compensation Examples

Publisher Status Reported Earnings
Joined at program start Over $1 million in a year
Joined a few months ago Around $50,000 to $60,000

💡 Why it matters

Google is facing scrutiny regarding the impact of its AI features on web traffic. This comes alongside regulatory actions:

  • In June, the UK ruled that Google must allow publishers to opt out of appearing in AI search features.
  • The European Union has opened an investigation into the impact on web traffic and ordered Google to make changes to its search engine.

#Google #AI #Publishing #Gemini #Search

Source: Google reportedly tests paying publishers for AI search results
